The red flag

Laps 26 to 34. A crash, a Safety Car, then the race stops for 16 minutes and every team gets a free set of tyres. Red Bull takes new mediums. Ferrari keeps the hards. Rosso, the strategist, gets its first say.

    Compressing the stoppage

    The race was stopped for 965.9 s. Auto speed runs it at 20×, the red clock keeps the real time, and the scrubber shades the stoppage.

    The tyre reveal

    When each team fitted its tyres isn't in the data, so the tower changes each car's tyre when it leaves the pit lane. That's also when the rivals found out.

    Rosso, the strategist

    First appearance. It only uses what the pit wall could see on lap 30. What happened later sits below it, clearly labelled, once the race gets there.

    Calm version

    No camera moves, trails, pop-up cards or animated reasoning. The tower still updates and Rosso reads as plain text.

    Car positions, lap times, pit lane times, tyres and race control messages from FastF1. Running order and gaps are worked out from car positions, so they can differ from the official tower by a few tenths. The Safety Car's position isn't in the data and is drawn as an estimate. Pit wall cards and the strategist are my reading of the data, not real team radio. Latifi's tyres are corrected from Pirelli's official chart. Personal concept, not affiliated with Formula 1 or Scuderia Ferrari.
